## Summary

The pitch, core verbatim: "Someone open-sourced a full library of backtested trading bots. Code included. Free. Every bot is one classic rule turned into a routine that runs on its own." Six bots, "25 years of daily data. Fees included." "Best one: RSI Reversion, +133% with a 75% win rate. And they even show the loser. RSI Dip: −27.9%. No cherry-picking." "The Python code is right there, so you can check every number yourself." CTA: "Drop the strategy you like into Claude, have it walk you through the code, then plug it into your Grok trading bot. Paper trade first. Find a strategy → backtest it → turn it into a bot."

**What the video shows** — a single-page dashboard titled **"GrokBot — Strategy Library: Open-Source Trading Bots"**, subtitle: "Every Grok Bot here turns one classic trading rule into a scheduled routine: entry & exit orders, risk limits and a kill switch, plus a backtest dashboard and the code to check every number." Filter chips: search by name / idea / code / ID · Daily · Long only · Paper first · Risk cap; type filters Trend (3) / Reversion (2) / Breakout (1), each clicked in turn ("Showing 6/6 → 3/6 → 2/6 → 1/6"); a sort switch Default order / By return / By drawdown. The footer line in every state: **"Showing 6/6 bots · one set of daily data, 25 years, 5 bp per side."** The header also shows a date `2026.11.02` (likely the data-as-of date) and, on the poster frame, unlabelled counters `479 · +26 · +75.0%` (plausibly repo stars and recent growth — unverified). The instrument behind "one set of daily data" is **never named** anywhere on the page.

**The six bots, steady-state table** (Return = cumulative over 25 years; "Annual" = CAGR):

| Bot | Type · order | Rule (dashboard text) | Return | Annual | Sharpe | Max DD | Win rate | P/L |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SMA Crossover Bot | Trend · market | Buys when SMA(20) crosses above SMA(50), sells on the reverse | +79.81% | +2.37% | 0.24 | −47.03% | 45.5% | 1.51 |
| RSI Reversion Bot | Reversion · market | Buys when RSI(14) drops below 35, sells back above 60 | **+133.01%** | +3.44% | 0.38 | −24.85% | **75.0%** | 2.24 |
| RSI Dip Bot | Reversion · limit | When RSI turns weak, places a limit buy 1% below the close | −27.92% | −1.30% | −0.12 | −36.76% | 50.0% | 0.87 |
| Trend Pullback Bot | Trend · limit | In an uptrend, waits for a 1% pullback from the high to enter | +120.78% | +3.22% | 0.31 | −29.63% | 30.8% | 1.76 |
| Breakout Bot | Breakout · stop | Stop buy at the 20-day high, exits below the 10-day low | +96.91% | +2.75% | 0.30 | −26.47% | 45.9% | 1.41 |
| Stop-Loss Bot | Trend · market + stop | Enters with the trend, every position gets a 5% protective stop | +78.44% | +2.34% | 0.24 | −40.93% | 24.1% | 1.33 |

Internal consistency: the Annual column is exactly the 25-year CAGR of the Return column (e.g. 1.3301^(1/25) = 1.0344), which confirms the headline "+133%" is a **25-year cumulative**, not an annual figure. Sorted by return the order is RSI Reversion > Trend Pullback > Breakout > SMA Crossover > Stop-Loss > RSI Dip. Each bot also has a detail card with Run / Dashboard buttons and the same footer "25 yrs daily · 5 bp/side".

## Why it matters

- **The headline number is a quarter-century total.** The tweet leads with "+133% with a 75% win rate"; the dashboard's own table says that is **3.44%/yr**, and the *best* of six bots carries a Sharpe of 0.38. The full range is −1.3% to +3.4% per year against max drawdowns of −25% to −47%. The most-liked reply (@young746, roughly as many likes as the tweet itself in the public page render, ~1.1k vs 1.2k) does this arithmetic: the best bot loses to doing nothing in the S&P (~5.5–6%/yr price-only over the same window, more with dividends), and "most of the others make 2.3–2.8%/yr with 25–47% drawdowns." The audience caught it within the day. "No cherry-picking" is only half true — showing one loser out of six textbook rules is candour about a curated set, not evidence against selection.
- **The one fact needed to judge it is missing: which market.** "One set of daily data, 25 years" is unnamed in the tweet, the page and the recording. Five bp per side is an equity-like cost assumption; nothing is said about slippage, dividends, or whether the limit/stop orders three of the bots depend on actually fill. Not evaluable from the capture.
- **"Code included. Free." could not be verified at capture.** No repo link exists in the text, the video or the quote; the page's `Link` buttons are never followed on camera; GitHub search found nothing. The only public code under sopersone's own GitHub is unrelated (a personal RSI+EMA spot bot forked from the Investing Algorithm Framework), so "someone" is a third party.
- **What is transferable is the packaging pattern, not the numbers:** one classic rule → one scheduled routine with entry/exit orders, risk limits and a kill switch, plus a per-bot backtest dashboard, paper-first, long-only, daily bars. That is the same "strategy as a pluggable file behind a shared risk skeleton" shape the quoted article argues for with *151 Trading Strategies* formulas, and the same funnel as the algojan Roboquant listings: free code whose showcase numbers are one configuration on one regime. The vault already holds every one of these six rule families with better documentation — SMA/ATR systems ([[2026-08-29-three-simple-ma-atr-systems]]), RSI mean-reversion ([[2026-08-30-quantified-strategies-rsi-adx-ibs]], [[2026-08-30-milk-man-dip-buy-rules]]), breakouts ([[2026-10-01-systematicpeter-breakout-equity-high]], [[2026-08-30-ignis-trend-following-realtest]]), pullbacks ([[2026-11-19-algojan-vwap-pullback-topstep-mnq]]) — so the library is a convenience wrapper, not new edge.
- **A note on the 75% win rate:** a high hit-rate with a 0.38 Sharpe and a −25% drawdown is the textbook mean-reversion signature — many small wins, fewer larger losses — not evidence of a robust edge. And the Stop-Loss Bot's "5% protective stop" still sits on a −40.9% max drawdown at a 24.1% win rate: the stop caps each loss, not the equity curve.
- **Verdict:** reference-grade as a *pattern* (six rules, one skeleton, a dashboard per bot), sub-cash as *performance*, unverifiable as *code* until the repo is located. The bar for anything further is [[2026-08-29-milk-man-replication-metrics]]; the reason published showcases get read with gates is [[2026-09-04-systematicpeter-why-publish-research]].
- **For the user:** filed as both — one Inbox task to locate the repo and run the checks that would settle it (instrument, rule-to-code fidelity, an OOS split on RSI Reversion and Trend Pullback). Any paper-trade decision belongs to the trading desk (separate company), not this vault.
